transliteration_key.g: ق (تُنطق g في العراق) وكذلك گ

dialogue.speaker: Zainab
dialogue.english: Good morning, Ali.

dialogue.speaker: Ali
dialogue.english: Good morning, how are you today?

dialogue.speaker: Zainab
dialogue.english: Good, but I'm still a bit sleepy.

dialogue.speaker: Ali
dialogue.english: Did you get up early?

dialogue.speaker: Zainab
dialogue.english: Yes, I got up at six.

dialogue.speaker: Ali
dialogue.english: It's a quarter past seven.

dialogue.speaker: Ali
dialogue.arabic: لازم أطلع للشغل هسة، ما عندي وگت.
dialogue.transliteration: laazim aTla3 lish-shughul hessa, ma 3indi wagit.
dialogue.english: I have to leave for work now, I don't have time.

dialogue.speaker: Zainab
dialogue.english: Do you want tea before you leave?

dialogue.speaker: Ali
dialogue.english: Yes, but quickly.

dialogue.speaker: Zainab
dialogue.english: Here, drink your tea, God be with you.

dialogue.speaker: Ali
dialogue.english: Thank you, see you in the evening.

response.english: Yes, I got up at six.

pair.english: Do you want coffee first thing?

response.arabic: إي أكيد، ما اگدر بلا گهوة
response.transliteration: ee akeed, ma agdar bala gahwa
response.english: Yes of course, I can't manage without coffee.

lessons.culture: Iraqis answer "صباح الخير" with "صباح النور" (or "صباح الورد"), and most people start the day with a glass of strong sweet چاي, while گهوة is more the drink for guests and gatherings. Someone leaving the house is often sent off with "الله وياك".

exercises.prompt: Someone says to you: "صباح الخير". Reply naturally.

too_formal.item: صباح الخير عليكم ورحمة الله وبركاته
too_formal.feedback: Correct, but much more elaborate than the everyday morning reply.

exercises.tip: The fixed everyday reply to "صباح الخير" is "صباح النور".

exercises.prompt: Someone asks you: "شكد الساعة هسة؟" Answer that it's seven o'clock.

too_formal.feedback: A bookish way to say the time; nobody says it like this out loud.

exercises.tip: "الساعة + number" is the everyday pattern for telling time.

exercises.prompt: Complete the sentence: "اريد _____ اول شي." English meaning: I want coffee first thing.

too_formal.feedback: Correct meaning, but wordier than the simple everyday word.

exercises.tip: Baghdadis say the ق of "قهوة" as g, so it is often written "گهوة".

exercises.prompt: Complete the sentence: "الصبح بدري هواية _____." English meaning: Early morning is very cold.

too_formal.feedback: Correct, but reads like a written weather report.

exercises.tip: "هواية" means "a lot" and is one of the most Iraqi words you can learn.

exercises.prompt: Translate into Iraqi Arabic: "I woke up early."

too_formal.feedback: This is correct Modern Standard Arabic, not how it is said in Baghdadi speech.

exercises.tip: "گمت" (I got up) is the everyday Iraqi verb; "صحيت" also works.

exercises.prompt: Translate: "I missed the bus."

too_formal.feedback: Grammatical but far too formal for everyday complaining about a bus.

exercises.tip: "فاتني" is used for missing a bus, a train, or any chance that passed.

exercises.prompt: Translate: "I'm still sleepy."

too_formal.feedback: Textbook Arabic; "بعدني" is the natural Iraqi word for "still".

exercises.tip: "بعدني" + adjective means "I'm still ..."; a woman says نعسانة.

exercises.prompt: Which sentence means "I left for work"?

too_formal.feedback: Correct meaning, but written-style Arabic, not the spoken phrase being practised.

exercises.tip: "طلعت" literally means "I went out".

exercises.prompt: Which reply fits "صباح الخير" best?

too_formal.feedback: Just repeating "صباح الخير" back sounds stiff; a real reply changes the word.

exercises.tip: "صباح النور" and "صباح الورد" are both natural replies.

exercises.prompt: Put these words in a natural order: "بدري / للشغل / طلعت"

too_formal.feedback: Correct meaning, but this word order and vocabulary belong to written Arabic.

exercises.tip: Verb, then place, then time is the natural spoken order here.

reply.english: At the restaurant in front of work.

phrases.arabic: لازم اخلص هذا الشغل گبل الظهر
phrases.transliteration: laazim akhallis haadha ish-shughul gabl iZ-Zuhur

dialogue.speaker: Hussain
dialogue.english: Hi Noor, what's up?

dialogue.speaker: Noor
dialogue.arabic: هلا حسين، وصلت للشغل هسة، وعندي هواية شغل.
dialogue.transliteration: hala Huseen, wuSalit lish-shughul hessa, w 3indi hawaaya shughul.
dialogue.english: Hi Hussain, I just arrived at work and I have a lot to do.

dialogue.speaker: Hussain
dialogue.english: Do you have a meeting today?

dialogue.speaker: Noor
dialogue.english: Yes, I have a meeting at ten.

dialogue.speaker: Hussain
dialogue.arabic: وآني لازم اخلص هذا الشغل گبل الظهر.
dialogue.transliteration: w aani laazim akhallis haadha ish-shughul gabl iZ-Zuhur.
dialogue.english: And I have to finish this task before noon.

dialogue.speaker: Noor
dialogue.english: Where are you having lunch today?

dialogue.speaker: Hussain
dialogue.arabic: بالمطعم گدام الشغل، جوعان من هسة.
dialogue.transliteration: bil-maT3am guddaam ish-shughul, joo3aan min hessa.
dialogue.english: At the restaurant in front of work, I'm hungry already.

dialogue.speaker: Noor
dialogue.arabic: آني هم جوعانة، بس اريد اخلص اول.
dialogue.transliteration: aani hamm joo3aana, bas areed akhalliS awwal.
dialogue.english: I'm hungry too, but I want to finish first.

dialogue.speaker: Hussain
dialogue.english: One moment, I'm looking for my pen.

dialogue.speaker: Noor
dialogue.english: It's on the desk in front of you.

dialogue.speaker: Hussain
dialogue.english: Ah, thanks, bless you.

dialogue.speaker: Noor
dialogue.arabic: أدگ عليك بعد الظهر ونروح نتغدى.
dialogue.transliteration: adugg 3aleek ba3d iZ-Zuhur w nirooH nitghadda.
dialogue.english: I'll call you in the afternoon and we'll go to lunch.

response.english: At the restaurant in front of work.

pair.english: Do you have a meeting today?

lessons.culture: In Iraq lunch (الغدا) is the main meal of the day, usually eaten in the early afternoon, and a break at work almost always comes with a glass of چاي. Colleagues often open a chat with "شكو ماكو؟" before getting to work.

exercises.prompt: Someone asks you: "وين تتغدى؟" Say you eat at the restaurant in front of work.

too_formal.item: أتناول الغداء في المطعم المجاور للعمل
too_formal.feedback: Correct, but a written-style sentence nobody says in reply.

exercises.tip: In speech people answer with just the place: "بالمطعم".

exercises.prompt: Someone asks you: "شنو الأخبار اليوم؟" Say there is nothing new.

too_formal.feedback: Correct, but "ماكو" is the everyday Iraqi word for "there isn't".

exercises.tip: "ماكو" means "there is not" and its opposite "أكو" means "there is".

exercises.prompt: Complete the sentence: "_____ اجتماع الساعة عشرة." English meaning: I have a meeting at ten.

too_formal.feedback: Correct in writing, but Iraqis say "عندي" for "I have".

exercises.tip: "عندي" is "I have" (literally "at me").

exercises.prompt: Complete the sentence: "اگدر آخذ _____؟" English meaning: Can I take a break?

too_formal.feedback: Correct, but a formal way to ask.

exercises.tip: "اگدر" is "can I": the ق of "أقدر" is said g.

exercises.prompt: Translate into Iraqi Arabic: "I arrived at work."

too_formal.feedback: This is correct Modern Standard Arabic, not how it is said in Baghdadi speech.

exercises.tip: "للشغل" is "لـ" + "الشغل" joined together.

exercises.prompt: Translate: "I have a lot of work now."

too_formal.feedback: This is correct Modern Standard Arabic, not how it is said in Baghdadi speech.

exercises.tip: "هواية" for "a lot" and "هسة" for "now" are the two words that make it sound Iraqi.

exercises.prompt: Translate: "I'll call you in the afternoon."

too_formal.feedback: This is correct Modern Standard Arabic, not how it is said in Baghdadi speech.

exercises.tip: "دگ على" (literally "knock on") is the everyday Iraqi way to say phone someone.

exercises.prompt: Which sentence means "I'm looking for my pen"?

too_formal.feedback: Correct, but "أبحث عن" is the written verb.

exercises.tip: "دوّر على" is "look for" in Iraqi speech.

exercises.prompt: Which question asks "Where do you have lunch?"

too_formal.feedback: Correct, but formal; "وين" is the spoken "where".

exercises.tip: "وين" means "where".

exercises.prompt: Put these pieces in order: "لازم / اخلص / هذا الشغل / گبل الظهر"
exercises.answer: لازم اخلص هذا الشغل گبل الظهر
accepted: لازم اخلص هذا الشغل گبل الظهر
لازم گبل الظهر اخلص هذا الشغل

too_formal.item: يجب أن أنهي هذه المهمة قبل الظهر
too_formal.feedback: This is correct Modern Standard Arabic, not how it is said in Baghdadi speech.

exercises.tip: "لازم" comes first and is followed by the bare verb.

dialogue.speaker: Mustafa
dialogue.english: Good evening, Sara.

dialogue.speaker: Sara
dialogue.english: Good evening, did you come back home?

dialogue.speaker: Mustafa
dialogue.arabic: إي، رجعت هسة، وتعبت هواية اليوم.
dialogue.transliteration: ee, rija3t hessa, w ti3abit hawaaya il-yoom.
dialogue.english: Yes, I just got back, and I got very tired today.

dialogue.speaker: Mustafa
dialogue.arabic: شي خفيف، بس اريد استحم اول.
dialogue.transliteration: shi khafeef, bas areed astaHimm awwal.
dialogue.english: Something light, but I want to shower first.

dialogue.speaker: Sara
dialogue.english: Fine, and shall we watch a series afterwards?

dialogue.speaker: Mustafa
dialogue.arabic: لا، خل نطلع نتمشى شوية، الجو حلو بالمسا.
dialogue.transliteration: laa, khal niTla3 nitmashsha shwayya, ij-jaww Hilu bil-masa.
dialogue.english: No, let's go out for a little walk, the weather is nice in the evening.

dialogue.speaker: Sara
dialogue.arabic: تمام، بس اريد أدگ على أهلي اول.
dialogue.transliteration: tamaam, bas areed adugg 3ala ahli awwal.
dialogue.english: Fine, but I want to call my family first.

dialogue.speaker: Mustafa
dialogue.english: Of course, take your time.

dialogue.speaker: Sara
dialogue.arabic: اليوم شفت ربعي بالمسا وگعدنا شوية.
dialogue.transliteration: il-yoom shift rab3i bil-masa w gi3adna shwayya.
dialogue.english: Today I saw my friends in the evening and we sat a while.

dialogue.speaker: Mustafa
dialogue.english: Nice, tonight I'll sleep early.

dialogue.speaker: Sara
dialogue.english: Good night.

dialogue.speaker: Mustafa
dialogue.english: And you.

pair.english: What will we eat for dinner?

lessons.culture: Iraqi evenings start late: dinner (العشا) is usually light, and cooler nights are for sitting outside, walking, or visiting relatives and friends. "ربعي" (my circle of friends) is the everyday Iraqi word for your friends, and good night is "تصبح على خير" answered "وانت من أهله".

exercises.prompt: Someone says to you: "مساء الخير". Reply naturally.

too_formal.feedback: Correct, but far more elaborate than the everyday evening reply.

exercises.tip: Like the morning, the reply changes the word: "مساء النور".

exercises.prompt: Someone says to you: "تصبح على خير". Reply naturally.

too_formal.feedback: Correct but a long, written-style reply.

exercises.tip: "وانت من أهله" is the fixed reply; a woman may say "وانتي".

exercises.prompt: Complete the sentence: "_____ راح نتعشى؟" English meaning: What will we eat for dinner?

too_formal.feedback: Correct, but "ماذا" is the written word for "what".

exercises.tip: "شنو" means "what" in Iraqi speech.

exercises.prompt: Complete the sentence: "اريد _____." English meaning: I want to shower.

too_formal.feedback: Correct, but stiff and written.

exercises.tip: "اريد" + a bare verb is the everyday way to say "I want to ...".

exercises.prompt: Translate into Iraqi Arabic: "I came back home."

too_formal.feedback: This is correct Modern Standard Arabic, not how it is said in Baghdadi speech.

exercises.tip: "رجعت" is "I came back"; "البيت" is the everyday word for home.

exercises.prompt: Translate: "I got very tired today."

too_formal.feedback: Correct, but "كثيرا" is the written word; Iraqis say "هواية".

exercises.tip: "هواية" after a verb means "a lot".

exercises.prompt: Translate: "I saw my friends in the evening."

too_formal.feedback: This is correct Modern Standard Arabic, not how it is said in Baghdadi speech.

exercises.tip: "شفت" is "I saw" and "ربعي" is "my friends".

exercises.prompt: Which sentence means "Let's go out for a little walk"?

too_formal.feedback: Correct meaning, but "دعنا" is written Arabic.

exercises.tip: "خل" + a verb is "let's ...".

exercises.prompt: Which word is the everyday Iraqi word for "my friends"?

too_formal.feedback: Correct, but "أصدقائي" is the written word.

exercises.tip: "ربعنا" means "our crowd" and is very Iraqi.

exercises.prompt: Put these words in a natural order: "بالمسا / حلو / الجو"

too_formal.feedback: This is correct Modern Standard Arabic, not how it is said in Baghdadi speech.

exercises.tip: "الجو" is the Iraqi word for the weather.

phrases.arabic: الأَحد، الاثنين، الثَّلاثَاء، الأَربِعَاء، الخَميس، الجُمعَة، السَّبت
phrases.transliteration: il-aHad, il-ithneen, ith-thalaatha, il-arba3aa, il-khamiis, ij-jum3a, is-sabt

phrases.arabic: الأسبوع الجَاي عِندنا اجتِمَاع يوم الثَّلاثَاء
اشتَغِل كُل يوم إِلا الجُمعَة والسَّبت

dialogue.speaker: Hassan
dialogue.arabic: هلا رقية، اليوم الأحد، أول يوم بالدوام.
dialogue.transliteration: hala ruqayya, il-yoom il-aHad, awwal yoom bid-dawaam.
dialogue.english: Hi Ruqayya, today is Sunday, the first day of work.

dialogue.speaker: Ruqayya
dialogue.english: Yes, and tomorrow is Monday, we have a meeting.

dialogue.speaker: Hassan
dialogue.arabic: لا، الاجتماع الأسبوع الجاي يوم الثلاثاء.
dialogue.transliteration: laa, il-ijtimaa3 il-usbuu3 ij-jaay yoom ith-thalaatha.
dialogue.english: No, the meeting is next week on Tuesday.

dialogue.speaker: Ruqayya
dialogue.english: Really? When exactly is the meeting?

dialogue.speaker: Hassan
dialogue.english: At ten in the morning.

dialogue.speaker: Ruqayya
dialogue.arabic: زين. يوم الأربعاء أشتغل لحد المسا.
dialogue.transliteration: zeen. yoom il-arba3aa ashtaghil laHad il-masa.
dialogue.english: Good. On Wednesday I work until the evening.

dialogue.speaker: Hassan
dialogue.transliteration: w aani yoom il-khamiis ashoof rab3i.
dialogue.english: And on Thursday I see my friends.

dialogue.speaker: Ruqayya
dialogue.arabic: آني اشتغل كل يوم إلا الجمعة والسبت.
dialogue.transliteration: aani ashtaghil kull yoom illa ij-jum3a w is-sabt.
dialogue.english: I work every day except Friday and Saturday.

dialogue.speaker: Hassan
dialogue.english: Friday is the day of prayer and rest.

dialogue.speaker: Ruqayya
dialogue.transliteration: ee, w shinu naawi tsawwi bil-3uTla?
dialogue.english: Yes, and what do you plan to do on the weekend?

dialogue.speaker: Hassan
dialogue.transliteration: yoom is-sabt nirooH lis-suug, w inti?
dialogue.english: On Saturday we go to the market, and you?

dialogue.speaker: Ruqayya
dialogue.english: I visit my family. The weekend comes quickly!

pair.english: What do you plan to do on the weekend?

response.english: No, Friday is a day off and rest.

pair.english: What do you do on Thursday?

lessons.culture: Iraq's working week runs Sunday to Thursday, and the weekend is Friday and Saturday. Friday is the day of the congregational prayer and of family time, and Saturday is a common day for the market (السوگ) and visiting relatives; "باچر" is tomorrow and "شوكت" is when.

exercises.prompt: Someone asks you: "شنو ناوي تسوي بالعطلة؟" Say you go to the market on Saturday.

too_formal.feedback: Correct, but written-style Arabic, not how people answer.

exercises.tip: "نروح" (we go) is also used for the near future.

exercises.prompt: Someone asks you: "شوكت الاجتماع؟" Say it is on Tuesday.

too_formal.feedback: Correct, but too long for a spoken reply.

exercises.tip: Just the day is a full answer: "يوم الثلاثاء".

exercises.prompt: Complete the sentence: "اليوم _____." English meaning: Today is Sunday.

too_formal.feedback: Correct, but too wordy.

exercises.tip: The Iraqi week starts on الأحد.

exercises.prompt: Complete the sentence: "_____ الاثنين." English meaning: Tomorrow is Monday.

too_formal.feedback: Correct, but "غدا" is the written word for tomorrow.

exercises.tip: "باچر" is the Iraqi word for tomorrow, with the چ sound.

exercises.prompt: Translate into Iraqi Arabic: "Tomorrow is Monday."

too_formal.feedback: This is correct Modern Standard Arabic, not how it is said in Baghdadi speech.

exercises.tip: No word for "is" is needed.

exercises.prompt: Translate: "On Thursday I see my friends."

too_formal.feedback: This is correct Modern Standard Arabic, not how it is said in Baghdadi speech.

exercises.tip: "أشوف" is "I see" in speech.

exercises.prompt: Translate: "The weekend comes quickly."

too_formal.feedback: This is correct Modern Standard Arabic, not how it is said in Baghdadi speech.

exercises.tip: "تجي" is "comes" and "العطلة" is the weekend or a day off.

exercises.prompt: Which day is "the day of prayer and rest"?

too_formal.feedback: Correct, but a fuller written phrase.

exercises.tip: الجمعة and السبت are the Iraqi weekend.

exercises.prompt: Which question asks "When is the meeting?"

too_formal.feedback: Correct, but "متى" is the written word for when.

exercises.tip: "شوكت" means "when" in Baghdad.

exercises.prompt: Put these pieces in order: "اشتغل / كل يوم / إلا / الجمعة والسبت"
exercises.answer: اشتَغِل كُل يوم إِلا الجُمعَة والسَّبت
accepted: اشتَغِل كُل يوم إِلا الجُمعَة والسَّبت
كل يوم اشتغل إلا الجمعة والسبت
ashtaghil kull yoom illa ij-jum3a w is-sabt

too_formal.item: أعمل كل يوم ما عدا الجمعة والسبت
too_formal.feedback: This is correct Modern Standard Arabic, not how it is said in Baghdadi speech.

exercises.tip: "إلا" introduces the exception.

challenge.title: Plan Your Week in Iraqi
challenge.instructions: Write and say a short conversation about a day and the week ahead, at least 10 lines. It must include a morning greeting and its reply, a question about the time, a statement about being tired or sleepy, an evening greeting and its reply, the good-night exchange, a question about when something happens, and a plan for the weekend. Use at least 8 target phrases from Unit 7.
required_elements: A morning greeting using صباح الخير and its reply صباح النور.
A statement about waking up or being sleepy, using گمت بدري or بعدني نعسان.
A question using شكد الساعة هسة؟ and a time answer.
A statement about being tired or having a lot of work, using تعبت هواية or عندي هواية شغل.
An evening greeting using مساء الخير and its reply مساء النور.
The good-night exchange using تصبح على خير and وانت من أهله.
A question using شوكت؟ and its answer.
A statement naming at least two days of the week.
A plan for the weekend using العطلة.
At least one invitation or suggestion, such as خل نطلع نتمشى.

dialogue.speaker: Zainab

dialogue.speaker: Ali

dialogue.speaker: Zainab

dialogue.speaker: Ali
dialogue.arabic: فكرة حلوة، بس اريد استحم اول.

dialogue.speaker: Zainab

dialogue.speaker: Ali
dialogue.arabic: يوم الخميس أشوف ربعي، ويوم السبت نروح للسوگ.

dialogue.speaker: Zainab

dialogue.speaker: Ali
